To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the range changes of British grasshoppers and cricket species between the 198os and the 200os were related to three of the four traits considered: ranges tended to have expanded for habitat generalists and for those with southerly distribution and ovipositing in vegetation.

1) the responses of species in a long-term distribution dataset to environmental change were dominated by two species, 2) these two species had an unusual combination of life history traits that may explain their rapid range expansion, and 3) trait-based analyses may provide insights into mechanisms underlying species responses to environmental changes, but results need careful interpretation and may have limited predictivity.
